text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi won support to send an Italian-led security force to Albania but at the cost of a rift with his hard-left Communist Refoundation allies that will expose the government to a confidence test in parliament. The Chamber of deputies voted by 503 to 85 with seven abstensions to deploy the multinational force, yet Prodi needed the backing of the centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance to secure the victory on a joint resolution (all).

* Deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni said Prodi's government next challenge, after European economic and monetary union and the Albanian crisis, was reform of the welfare state. (Corriere della Sera).

* Giorgio Fossa, president of industrialists' association Confindustria, said the government's economic policy harmed industries by not cutting public spending, thus endangering Italy's future not only in an EMU framework but also as an industrialised country (all).

* Post and telecommunications minister Antonio Maccanico signed a decree law due to privatise Italian telecoms sector by January 1, 1998 following the European rules. Maccanico also met the heads of France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom (all).
* State telecoms holding Stet will sell its 48.9 percent in cable-laying company Sirti by this summer, before merging with Telecom Italia and its own privatisation (Sole 24 Ore).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
